issues.display_title: Issue #502: Send Centrifugo WebSocket Notification on PostComplete Worker
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Send Centrifugo WebSocket Notification on PostComplete Worker

Summary

Integrated Centrifugo WebSocket notifications into the PostComplete worker (src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go) in panorra-api-go-new. When a panorama post finishes processing and is marked as published, the worker dispatches a real-time event directly to the author's dedicated Centrifugo channel (publish_post:<username>) alongside existing push notifications. Unit tests were added in PostComplete_test.go verifying error handling, HTTP payload structure, authorization headers, and channel naming.

Additionally, a dedicated test endpoint was introduced in panorra-api-go (/centrifugo/publish-post/:username) without authentication requirements to allow quick, dynamic end-to-end testing of the WebSocket event.

Files Updated

1. panorra-api-go-new (Worker Implementation)

  • src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go:

    • Imported "net/http".
    • Added publishCentrifugo(endpoint, apiKey, channel string, data map[string]interface{}, client *http.Client) error: Dispatches POST request to Centrifugo API with apiKey authorization and a 5-second timeout.
    • Added sendCentrifugoPublishPost(username string, data map[string]interface{}) error: Wraps publishing to publish_post:<username>.
    • Integrated into the worker publication block (if existingNotifCount == 0) with payload containing:
      • slug: post identifier.
      • description: post description.
      • thumbnail: default thumbnail URL.
      • location: location coordinates and place data.
    • Added safe error logging via Functions.SaveLogErr to prevent worker stalls if Centrifugo is temporarily unreachable.

  • src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete_test.go:

    • TestPublishCentrifugo_MissingConfig: Verifies error on missing endpoint or API key.
    • TestPublishCentrifugo_Success: Verifies HTTP request headers, JSON body, and channel payload.
    • TestPublishCentrifugo_HttpError: Verifies non-200 HTTP response detection.
    • TestSendCentrifugoPublishPost_ChannelFormat: Verifies publish_post:<username> format.

2. panorra-api-go (Testing Endpoint)

  • src/Action/V1/Centrifugo/TestPublishPost.go:
    • Public testing handler without auth requirements (c.Params("username")).
    • Supports optional query parameters or request body overrides (slug, description, thumbnail, location) with fallback mock data.
    • Dispatches payload directly to Centrifugo channel publish_post:<username>.
  • src/Controllers/V1/CentrifugoControllers.go:
    • Added TestPublishPost controller delegation.
  • src/Routes/V1/CentrifugoRoutes.go:
    • Registered GET and POST routes on default route /centrifugo/publish-post/:username.
  • src/Action/V1/Centrifugo/Centrifugo_test.go:
    • Added comprehensive unit tests covering config validation, successful publish, and request body overrides.

Centrifugo WebSocket Channel & Payload Specifications

  • Channel: publish_post:<username> (e.g., publish_post:johndoe)
  • Event Payload Structure:
{
  "channel": "publish_post:johndoe",
  "data": {
    "slug": "c9e2b10a-202609210001",
    "description": "360 Panorama at Mount Bromo",
    "thumbnail": "https://storage.panorra.com/posts/c9e2b10a/thumb.jpg",
    "location": {
      "place_name": "Mount Bromo, East Java",
      "latitude": -7.942494,
      "longitude": 112.953012
    }
  }
}

Quick Test Guide

To quickly verify that the frontend / client receives the WebSocket notification without needing to trigger the entire panorama upload and transcoding pipeline, use the public test endpoint on panorra-api-go.

Step 1: Subscribe on Client / Centrifugo Web UI

In frontend / test client, subscribe to the user's channel:

const sub = centrifuge.newSubscription("publish_post:johndoe");

sub.on('publication', function(ctx) {
    console.log("Received post publication event:", ctx.data);
    // ctx.data contains: { slug, description, thumbnail, location }
});

sub.subscribe();

Step 2: Trigger Event via Quick Test Endpoint

Option A: Quick Test via Browser or cURL (GET)

Hit the endpoint directly with just the target username:

curl {{base_url}}/centrifugo/publish-post/johndoe

With custom query parameters:

curl "{{base_url}}/centrifugo/publish-post/johndoe?slug=bromo-360&description=Sunset+view"

Option B: Custom Payload Test via cURL / Postman (POST)

curl -X POST {{base_url}}/centrifugo/publish-post/johndoe \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "slug": "custom-post-sid-999",
    "description": "Sunrise at Mount Bromo",
    "thumbnail": "https://panorra.com/assets/images/sample.jpg",
    "location": {
      "place_name": "Mount Bromo",
      "latitude": -7.942494,
      "longitude": 112.953012
    }
  }'

Expected API Response (HTTP 200):

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "message": "Centrifugo websocket publish_post sent successfully",
    "channel": "publish_post:johndoe",
    "data": {
      "slug": "custom-post-sid-999",
      "description": "Sunrise at Mount Bromo",
      "thumbnail": "https://panorra.com/assets/images/sample.jpg",
      "location": {
        "place_name": "Mount Bromo",
        "latitude": -7.942494,
        "longitude": 112.953012
      }
    }
  }
}

Verification

1. panorra-api-go-new

go test -v ./src/Worker/PostComplete/...
go vet ./src/Worker/PostComplete/...

Output:

  • All 5 unit tests passed cleanly (including 4 new Centrifugo tests).
  • Static analysis completed with 0 errors.

2. panorra-api-go

go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Centrifugo/...
go vet ./src/...

Output:

  • All 5 unit tests passed cleanly.
  • Static analysis completed with 0 errors.

Problem

When the PostComplete background worker (src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go) finished processing a published panorama post, it only sent mobile and web push notifications to the author. However, modern single-page applications (web) and mobile apps require real-time WebSocket feedback to immediately transition the UI (e.g., closing upload loaders, updating feed status, or redirecting to the newly published panorama) without waiting for background push notifications or polling APIs.

Furthermore, sending post-completion events over a global broadcast channel (like publish_post with client-side username filtering) poses privacy risks (data leakage to third-party observers inspecting WebSockets) and excessive network overhead (broadcasting to thousands of idle subscribers).

Scope

  • Add Centrifugo WebSocket publishing helper functions in src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go:
    • publishCentrifugo: Generic helper to dispatch signed JSON messages to Centrifugo HTTP API (ENDPOINT_CENTRIFUGO, APIKEY_CENTRIFUGO) with a 5-second HTTP client timeout.
    • sendCentrifugoPublishPost: Scopes channel targeting specifically to publish_post:<username> to ensure strict private delivery.
  • Integrate Centrifugo publishing into PostComplete.go:
    • Trigger right after successful post publication alongside the push notification block.
    • Deliver payload containing slug, description, thumbnail, and location.
    • Safely log any Centrifugo connection errors without interrupting downstream Redis cleanup or subscriber notification workers.
  • Add comprehensive unit tests in src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete_test.go:
    • TestPublishCentrifugo_MissingConfig: Verifies error handling when endpoint or API key is unset.
    • TestPublishCentrifugo_Success: Verifies HTTP request headers (Authorization: apiKey ..., Content-Type: application/json), payload format, and HTTP 200 response handling.
    • TestPublishCentrifugo_HttpError: Verifies non-200 HTTP response detection.
    • TestSendCentrifugoPublishPost_ChannelFormat: Verifies channel naming convention publish_post:<username>.

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% backward compatible: retains existing mobile push (ExpoNotification), web push (NotificationWeb), and database notification inserts.
  • Non-blocking: if Centrifugo is unreachable, the worker logs the error to database logs (Functions.SaveLogErr) and safely continues execution (does not cause message requeue or post deletion).
  • Targeted delivery: WebSocket message is published strictly to the post author's channel (publish_post:<username>).

Out of Scope

  • Changing database schemas or push notification delivery services.
  • Modifying client-side WebSocket client library configurations.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Centrifugo publishing helpers added to src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go.
  • Channel formatted as publish_post:<username>.
  • Payload includes slug, description, thumbnail, and location.
  • Unit tests pass cleanly (go test -v ./src/Worker/PostComplete/...).
  • Project builds cleanly with no compilation or vet errors.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-21.

Implementation: Consolidate User Social Relations

Summary

Consolidated repetitive user lookup, blocking verification, Redis cache synchronization, and block cleanup logic across the social interaction endpoints in src/Action/V1/Users/ (FollowUser.go, BlockUser.go, SubscribeUser.go, ReportUser.go). Introduced social_helpers.go accompanied by unit tests in social_helpers_test.go, streamlining all social interaction handlers while strictly preserving exact flow and response contracts.

Files Updated

1. New Helper Module and Tests in src/Action/V1/Users/

  • social_helpers.go:
    • findUserByUsername: Reusable target user lookup by username.
    • isUserBlocked: Checks if a mutual block exists between two users.
    • syncSocialSuggestions: Safely invalidates and refreshes suggestion caches in Redis.
    • syncBlockCache: Safely refreshes blocked user lists and suggestions in Redis.
    • cleanupBookmarksAndFollowersOnBlock: Deletes mutual bookmarks, updates ElasticSearch totals, and removes mutual follow records.
    • respondSocialSlimOrPlain: Standardizes encrypted responses for slim clients (sl=true) and standard responses.
  • social_helpers_test.go:
    • TestSyncSocialHelpersSafeWithoutRedis: Verifies that cache sync helpers execute safely without panics when Redis is uninitialized.

2. Refactored Handlers in src/Action/V1/Users/

  • FollowUser.go: Streamlined target user lookup, mutual block check, Redis suggestions sync, and slim response encryption.
  • BlockUser.go: Replaced ~50 lines of inline bookmark and follower cleanup with cleanupBookmarksAndFollowersOnBlock, and unified response encryption.
  • SubscribeUser.go: Streamlined target user lookup and mutual block check.
  • ReportUser.go: Streamlined target user lookup and duplicate active report upserting.

Verification

go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Users/...
go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Notifications/...
go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Likes/...
go test -v ./src/Utils/Functions/...
go build ./...
  • All unit tests in src/Action/V1/Users/ passed cleanly.
  • All test suites across the repository passed.
  • Entire repository compiled cleanly with go build ./... (0 errors).

Problem

The user social interaction handlers in src/Action/V1/Users/ (FollowUser.go, BlockUser.go, SubscribeUser.go, and ReportUser.go) contained repetitive logic and duplicated queries:

  1. Target User Lookups: Each handler performed identical database lookups for the target user by username with redundant record presence checks.
  2. Mutual Blocking Verification: Checking whether two users block each other (UserFunctions.CheckBlockingUser) was copied verbatim across multiple handlers.
  3. Redis Social Cache Invalidation: Updating Redis suggestion caches (Redis.SuggestionUser) and blocked user lists (Redis.ListBlockUser) was duplicated.
  4. Block Cleanup Operations: Deleting shared bookmarks, updating ElasticSearch counters, and removing bidirectional follow rows occupied ~40 lines in BlockUser.go.
  5. Response Formatting & Encryption: Encrypting slim responses (sl=true) was identical between FollowUser.go and BlockUser.go.

Scope

  • Create shared helper functions in src/Action/V1/Users/social_helpers.go:
    • findUserByUsername: Reusable lookup of user ID, username, and encrypt token.
    • isUserBlocked: Encapsulates mutual blocking check via UserFunctions.CheckBlockingUser.
    • syncSocialSuggestions: Reusable trigger for suggestion cache refresh.
    • syncBlockCache: Refreshes blocked user lists and suggestions in Redis with nil-safety.
    • cleanupBookmarksAndFollowersOnBlock: Encapsulates removing shared bookmarks, updating ElasticSearch, and deleting mutual followers.
    • respondSocialSlimOrPlain: Standardizes slim encrypted vs plain JSON responses.
  • Add unit tests in src/Action/V1/Users/social_helpers_test.go.
  • Refactor handlers:
    • FollowUser.go: Use shared user lookup, block verification, suggestions sync, and slim response helper.
    • BlockUser.go: Use shared user lookup, block cleanup, cache sync, and slim response helper.
    • SubscribeUser.go: Use shared user lookup and block verification.
    • ReportUser.go: Use shared user lookup and self-action check.
  • Retain uppercase step comments (// COMMENT) and function headers (// ===================================//).

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% backward compatible: maintains exact status codes, error messages (including casing nuances like "User Not Found" vs "User not found"), database transactions, ElasticSearch counter updates, and JSON response envelopes.
  • Zero changes to response contracts for frontend clients.

Out of Scope

  • Modifying bookmark database models, follower schemas, or report categorization.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Shared social helpers created with unit test coverage.
  • FollowUser.go, BlockUser.go, SubscribeUser.go, and ReportUser.go refactored and deduplicated.
  • All unit tests pass (go test ./src/Action/V1/Users/...).
  • Project builds cleanly (go build ./...).

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-18.
